subject: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@paragonretail.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paragonretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit

Hi Jamie & Sanjay,

Thanks again for the conversation last week — really appreciate the transparency on Q1 usage patterns and the team roadmap (especially around the recommender rollout). Based on Paragon's target ramp and the feature adoption you described, attached is a concise renewal proposal that aims to:

- keep your unit price flat for the next 12 months (price hold) conditioned on a stepped commit ramp,
- provide a temporary overage credit pool for the first 90 days post renew to smooth onboarding spikes, and
- include a small adoption credit tied to successful rollout of the recommender feature across two regions (details in the spreadsheet).

Key bullets:
- 12-month term, 3 quarterly true-ups (quarterly committed token thresholds in commit_ramp_model.xlsx)
- Price hold at current effective rate through term if quarterly commit thresholds are met; if a quarter falls short, price reverts only for that quarter to the standard list (no retroactive), and Paragon receives a one-time smoothing credit capped at $25k for the shortfall.
- SLA-linked credit: if avg 95th percentile p99 latency exceeds 450ms more than twice in a quarter, automatic credit equal to 2% of that quarter's invoice for the impacted route.
- DocuSign-ready amendment (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf) attached — legal redlines are minimal.

Ben and Markus are on this thread for ops and legal/finance alignment. Would love to get you an initial yes/no by end of next week so we can lock capacity in us-west.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: paragon_renewal_proposal_v1.pdf (pdf), commit_ramp_model.xlsx (xlsx), proposed_amendment_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Jamie Park <jamie@paragonretail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paragonretail.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit

Naomi — thanks for the proposal and for laying out the SLA/credit language clearly. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering before we take this to finance:

1) For the quarterly thresholds, can you confirm how you treat burst traffic in month 1 of each quarter? Our holiday planning may create large short spikes.
2) The $25k cap on smoothing credit — procurement is asking for a tiered cap (e.g., $25k for tier 1, $50k for tier 2) depending on whether the shortfall occurs in the ramp quarter vs. later.
3) Can we get a direct example of the invoice math if we hit 85% of committed tokens in a quarter?

Also, legal flagged the SLA credit language as a bit vague around "impacted route" — can we make that explicit (api-chat vs embeddings)?

Jamie
VP, Cloud Engineering — Paragon Retail
jamie@paragonretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit

Naomi / Markus — forwarding Jamie's questions. Ops note: burst traffic in the first month is treated as part of the quarter bucket for commit accounting, but we currently do a 10% burst allowance for seasonal events if notified 14 days prior. That needs to be explicit in the amendment.

Markus — can you take a pass on the legal/SLA wording and the tiered smoothing credit? Priyom, please prepare an invoice example showing: committed, actual, shortfall, applied smoothing credit, and effective per-token price when 85% of commit is used. Attach the sample calc to the next reply.

-Ben

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@paragonretail.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit

Jamie — looping in updated language suggestions inline below and attaching a tracked-change PDF (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf). Summary of edits:

- Burst allowance: explicit 10% seasonal burst allowance per quarter if Redwood is notified at least 14 days in advance; unannounced bursts are billable as consumption.
- Tiered smoothing credit: 1) Ramp quarter shortfall: smoothing cap $50k; 2) Subsequent quarter shortfall: smoothing cap $25k. Caps are per fiscal quarter.
- Invoice math example included in commit_ramp_model.xlsx (tab "sample_calc"). If you hit 85% of committed tokens in the quarter, you pay for committed tokens at the held price, but receive a smoothing credit equal to min(cap, (committed - actual) * held_price). The example shows the effective blended per-token rate.
- SLA credit: specify impacted route (chat-generation route id: /v1/generate/chat) and embeddings route (/v1/embeddings) with separate credit buckets; credit triggers only when p99 > 450ms for the specific route on >= 2 calendar days in the quarter.

If this aligns, we can push a DocuSign envelope with the final amendment and a short SOW for the ramped capacity.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paragonretail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Jamie Park <jamie@paragonretail.com>
Cc: Maggie Li <maggie@paragonretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit

Thanks Naomi & Markus — that language looks workable. Two small asks from finance before we sign:

1) Can the smoothing credit be paid as an invoice-level credit (applied to the next invoice) rather than an adjustment to historical invoices?
2) We'd like a one-time onboarding credit (separate from smoothing) of $15k tied to Redwood support hours during the recommender go-live window.

If both are okay, I'll route to finance and get an approval queue started — likely 48–72 hours.

Sanjay
Director, Finance — Paragon Retail

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paragonretail.com>, Jamie Park <jamie@paragonretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: volume ramp, conditional price hold & usage-linked credit

Sanjay — great, yes to both asks.

- Smoothing credit will be issued as an invoice credit applied to the next invoice following the quarter shortfall.
- We will include a one-time onboarding support credit of $15k in the amendment and reflect the support-hour expectation in the SOW.

I'll update the DocuSign package this afternoon (link included above) and send a sign-by date of Sep 30 to secure the us-west capacity. If we need a slightly later signing window, let me know — we'll prioritize the onboarding support dates you require.

Thanks everyone — close loop once you sign and we'll schedule a technical kickoff with our solutions team.

—Naomi
